pr.title: feat(events): report machine size as a coarse band, not a core count
pr.body:
- Adds `cpu_band` to the common span attributes — a coarse machine-size band on every span, so "is this a server or someone's laptop" becomes answerable. `runtime_context` says *where* a process runs but has no capacity axis, and its largest bucket is a catch-all: a gunicorn worker on a VM and `python main.py > out.log` on a MacBook both report `non_interactive`; Docker Desktop on a laptop reports `container` via `/.dockerenv`; a Remote-SSH shell on a server reports `vscode_terminal`.
- No public API change. `crewai_core.runtime_env` is not re-exported from either package root, and `detect_cpu_band` is new — so unlike the moved detection helpers it gets no compatibility shim in `crewai.telemetry.utils`.
- **The `share_crew`-gated exact `cpus` attribute and the four `platform*` attributes are untouched.** That gating was a deliberate 2024 classification of machine fingerprint as shareable content (`44e38b1d5`, *"Fixing telemetry condition that was missing"*), and this does not reverse it: the band is a range; the precise value stays opt-in.
- Six bands, powers of two, top one open-ended — `1-2`, `3-4`, `5-8`, `9-16`, `17-32`, `33+`. Open-ended because the exact count *is* the fingerprint: the observed fleet maximum is 512, and a span reporting 512 identifies one machine. The vocabulary is closed and asserted, as for `KNOWN_CODING_AGENTS` and `KNOWN_RUNTIME_CONTEXTS`.
- Tests cover every band boundary inclusively (1/2/3/4/5/8/9/16/17/32/33/96/512), that the top band absorbs 512 rather than leaking it, that an unavailable count is `unknown` rather than silently `1-2`, that the real host lands in the closed vocabulary, that no emittable value can carry a precise count, and that it rides the common attributes rather than one span type.
- Docs updated in `en`/`ar`/`ko`/`pt-BR`, in the default-on **Execution Environment** row, stating explicitly that the band is a range and that the exact count remains opt-in under **Environment Information**. No `docs/v*/` touched.
- Keeps this intentionally small: no warehouse column in this PR (a new tag key is ignored by every existing extractor, so no consumer breaks and it can follow), no change to any existing attribute or gate, and no reduction of the gated `cpus`.
- Next: a `cpu_band` column on the crew spine, then item 4.7(iii).

**One trap documented in the docstring rather than left to be rediscovered:** `os.cpu_count()` reports **host** cores, not the cgroup quota, so a 1-vCPU pod on a 96-core node lands in `33+`. That is the right answer for "what kind of machine is this" and the wrong one for "what resources did this run get" — `os.process_cpu_count()` gives the latter but requires Python 3.13, above this package's 3.10 floor.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_01GzrA3L2EFh9pRFi7RqUpLf

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Documentation and additive anonymous telemetry only; no public API or changes to existing `share_crew` gates.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds default-on telemetry **`cpu_band`** on every span via `common_span_attributes()`, alongside existing execution-environment fields. **`detect_cpu_band()`** in `crewai_core.runtime_env` maps `os.cpu_count()` to a closed vocabulary (`1-2` through `17-32`, `33+`, or `unknown`) so fleet analytics can distinguish laptop-scale from server-scale hosts without emitting an exact core count.
> 
> The **`share_crew`-gated exact CPU count** under Environment Information is unchanged; docs in **en/ar/ko/pt-BR** now describe the band on the Execution Environment row and clarify that precise counts remain opt-in. Tests cover band boundaries, `unknown` when count is unavailable, vocabulary safety, and that **`cpu_band`** is a process-wide common attribute (not limited to crew-created spans).

* docs(telemetry): say where the cpu band comes from

The Execution Environment row ended "Detection reads only whether known
environment variables are set, never their values". True for the assistant
and runtime-context fields, and wrong for the band this PR adds:
detect_cpu_band() reads os.cpu_count() (runtime_env.py:306) and touches no
environment variable. In a privacy disclosure table that is the kind of
inaccuracy worth a line.

Names the source explicitly and scopes the env-var sentence to the two
fields it actually describes. All four locales at parity.

pt-BR also takes the reviewer's wording fix: "um de uma lista fixa" ->
"um valor de uma lista fixa", and the missing comma before o `project_id`.
